4.4 Forecasting Revenue v. Expenses

The model methodology outlined in Section 3, for billed revenue projections will be used to compare
forecasted revenue and expenses. Non-rate revenue will be projected with a 3% annual increase, and
this impact is reflected in the updated revenue projections.

e Table 4-4 presents the projected revenue and expenses if Cabot Waterworks transitions to
100% purchased water from CAW.

e Table 4-5 displays the projected revenue and expenses if Cabot Waterworks remains with the
current purchase agreement, continuing to purchase only 0.3 MGD of its total water use from
CAW. Unlike the 100% purchase scenario, O&M expenses will not decrease in this case, as
the costs associated with maintaining the existing groundwater infrastructure will persist.

The financial impact of transitioning to 100% purchased water from CAW versus maintaining the
current purchase agreement presents key differences:

e Transitioning to 100% purchased water significantly increases total expenses due to higher
purchased water volume, scheduled CAW rate increases, and additional fees such as the
Infrastructure Fee, Watershed Protection Fee, and Development Fee. As a result, a larger net
deficit is projected, particularly in 2026 when the full transition takes effect.

e Maintaining the current purchase agreement avoids the higher costs associated with 100%
purchased water by maintaining the existing groundwater system. While this scenario
reduces dependency on CAW’s rate structure, continued investment in infrastructure and
potential capital improvements may still be necessary.

While moving to fully purchased water simplifies operations, it comes at a higher financial cost.
Without rate adjustments, Cabot Waterworks will face growing deficits under both scenarios. Rising
costs for materials, fuel, and maintenance further strain financial stability. To account for inflation
and operational cost growth, a 4% annual increase has been applied to 2024’s recorded O&M
expenses outside of purchased water and public safety, as well as all general and administrative
(G&A) expenses. Public safety expenses will remain at 5% of water billed revenue plus $35,000 in
Lieu of City Taxes, while a 5% gross revenue allocation for repairs and refurbishments will also be
applied.

To maintain financial sustainability, a rate increase will be necessary to cover the rising cost of
purchased water. However, operating expenses, regulatory compliance, and_ infrastructure
investments are adequately funded under the current rate structure, provided there are no changes
to the purchase agreement with CAW.

5 WATER RATE INCREASE

Rising costs across multiple areas—including purchased water expenses, operations, maintenance,
and infrastructure—necessitate a rate adjustment to maintain financial stability. This section
presents two rate results scenarios to address these increasing expenses:

e Section 5.1 outlines the unit rate increase per customer for 100% purchased water
agreement.

e Section 5.2 outlines a rate increase if Cabot Waterworks transitions to purchasing 100% of
its water from CAW.

e Section 5.3 details the rate results if the utility maintains its current purchase agreement with
CAW, continuing to produce most of its water while purchasing a smaller portion.

e Section 5.4 provides a comparative analysis of the resulting average customer bills.

Through the water model projection process, various rate structures can be evaluated to assess their
financial impact. When considering rate adjustments, factors such as the effect on different
customer groups and the need to cover rising expenses—particularly in purchased water, operations,
and maintenance—must be addressed.

One approach is adjusting the unit rate, ensuring revenue aligns with increasing costs tied to water
consumption. Alternatively, incorporating these expenses into the Service Flat Charge, similar to the
debt service fee, may not fully account for the variable nature of purchased water and operational
costs. Another option is implementing targeted fees to address specific cost drivers.

Ultimately, the selected rate adjustments must enable Cabot Waterworks to meet its financial
obligations while maintaining reliable service and infrastructure.

5.1 Unit Rate Increase CAW

Table 5-1 presents the annual unit rate (cost per 1,000 gallons) from CAW, which is added to all
existing unit rate thresholds. This rate increases each year as purchased water costs rise.

To determine the unit cost, the shortfall revenue due to purchased water (Identified in Table 4-4) is
divided by the projected billed water volume and converted to a per-1,000-gallon basis. This ensures
that the necessary rate adjustments are applied to each customer class and unit rate threshold.

ORDINANCE NO. 15 OF 2026
AN ORDINANCE FIXING RATES, FEES, AND DEPOSITS FOR
WATER AND OTHER WATER SERVICES RENDERED BY THE
CABOT WATER AND WASTEWATER COMMISSION; AND FOR
OTHER PURPOSES
WHEREAS, Arkansas Code Annotated § 14-234-214 provides that the water rates for
customers of a municipal waterworks system shall be fixed by the legislative body of the
municipality; and
WHEREAS, the City of Cabot, Arkansas (the “City”) has delegated responsibility for the
operations of the water and wastewater systems to the Cabot Water and Wastewater Commission

(the “Commission” or “Utility”); and

WHEREAS, the Cabot Water and Wastewater Commission has conducted a Rate Study in
accordance with Arkansas Act 605 of 2021 to establish Water Rates. (Exhibit A).

WHEREAS, the Commission has requested that the City approve the schedule of rates to be
charged by the Commission for Water services for customers that receive the Commission’s Water

services and those that do not receive its water services.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
OF CABOT, ARKANSAS:

Section 1. Purpose. It is the purpose of this Ordinance to fix fair and reasonable water rates
and fees applicable to customers of the Cabot Water and Wastewater Commission.
Section 2. Definitions. When used in this Ordinance, the following words and phrases shall
have the meaning as indicated:
(a) Customer Service Rate Classification;

i. Residential is a type of water or wastewater use that is directly related to
the function of a home. Residential use does not include any use associated
with the operation of any business or enterprise whether or not such
business or enterprise is operated for profit, or any in-ground lawn

irrigation system.
--- page 36 (OCR) ---
ii. Commercial is any type of water or wastewater use other than Residential,
Wholesale, Irrigation, or Hydrant water, as those terms are defined herein.

iii. Irrigation is a type of water use primarily dedicated to providing water to
plants and lawns.

iv. Non-Water Customer means a customer of the Utility receiving
wastewater services only.

v. Non-Water Customer — With Trash means a customer of the Utility
receiving wastewater services only that also receives trash-pickup services
from the City or its designee.

(b) Cut-off Date means the 25" day of the month unless the 25" day falls on a
weekend or official City holiday, in which case, Cut-off Date shall mean the first working day
following the weekend or holiday.

(c) Delinquent account means a customer account that has been disconnected or
locked-off due to non-payment of charges, fees, penalties or other assessments.

(d) Disconnected means that a properly authorized individual has adjusted the
valve assembly on a customer’s water meter such that water will not flow through the meter.

(e) Due Date means the 15" day of the month unless the 15" day falls on a
weekend or official ity holiday, in which case, Due Date shall mean the first working day following
the weekend or holiday.

(f) Hydrant is a type of water use primarily dedicated to combating fires but may

also include bulk water such as that used during construction.

(g) Lock-off means that a properly authorized individual has affixed a lock to a

Disconnected meter that shall only be removed by an authorized individual.
--- page 37 (OCR) ---
(h) Minimum Monthly Charge is the least amount that shall be billed to each
and every customer regardless of the amount of water used.

(i) Multiple-Unit Installation is a water and wastewater system that is designed
such that more than one residence or commercial unit within a structure is served water through a
single meter; such as an apartment, duplex and strip mall. A minimum monthly charge will be
accessed on each unit in a multi-unit facility.

(j) Organization Fee is a non-refundable monthly charge applied to any and all
real estate companies, agencies, landlords, and contractors who desire to have water service
temporarily connected to a property that they manage for the purpose of cleaning, repairing, or
otherwise performing maintenance of the property. The Organization Fee does not include the cost
of water usage. The Organization Fee does not apply to new construction projects.

(k) Re-connection Fee is the fee that must be paid before the reconnection of a
previously disconnected meter for any reason.

() Renter means residential water or wastewater customers who own less than a
fee interest in the property that they occupy.

(m) Special Pricing Areas are locations within the City of Cabot where customers
are required to pay increased rates to reimburse the City of Cabot for certain infrastructure costs.

(n) Voluntarily Disconnected Meter is a residential or irrigation meter that has
been Disconnected or Locked-Off by the City at the customer’s request so that the customer may
forego monthly minimum charges. Customers whose meters are voluntarily disconnected will be
required to pay a re-connection fee before water service is restored.

(0) Water Customer means a customer of the Utility receiving water service

along with wastewater services.
--- page 38 (OCR) ---
(p) Wastewater means Sanitary Sewer and related service connections to
Wastewater Collection Pipes.

Section 3. Water Service Territory. The City Council hereby finds and declares that the

Commission is authorized to extend its water-service territory to include any properties for which
a water connection exists. Any and all fees for connections shall follow Exhibit C Fees. The Utility
shall not be responsible for the costs of a new water connection.

Section 4. Disparate Rates. The City Council hereby finds and declares that Water
Customers, Non-Water Customers, and Non- Water Customers — With Trash should proportionately
share in the costs associated with the administration of the Commission and water services; thus,
the monthly water rates charged to Water Customers, Non-Water Customers, and Non-Water
Customers — With Trash should properly allocate those costs.

Section 5. Water Rates. The City Council hereby finds and declares that the monthly water
rates that are set forth in Exhibit B, “Monthly Water Rate Chart,” which is attached hereto and
incorporated herein as if set forth word for word, are fair and reasonable and reflect the minimum
rates necessary to ensure the continued operation and growth of the Utility; thus the “Monthly Water
Rate Chart” is hereby adopted and the rates reflected therein are hereby fixed as the rates to be
charged for water services to be rendered by the Utility.

(a) City-Owned Facilities. All City-owned facilities shall be billed at the
Commercial rate classification set out in Exhibit B, regardless of whether such facility would
otherwise qualify for a different rate classification.

Section 6. Fees. The City Council hereby finds and declares that the fees that are set forth
in Exhibit C, “Fee Chart,” which is attached hereto and incorporated herein as if set forth word for

word, are fair and reasonable and reflect the minimum fees necessary to ensure the continued
--- page 39 (OCR) ---
operation and growth of the Utility; thus, the “Fee Chart” is hereby adopted and the fees reflected
therein are hereby fixed as the fees to be charged for various services to be rendered by the Utility.

Section 7. Deposits. The City Council hereby finds and declares that the deposits that are
set forth in Exhibit D, “Deposit Chart’, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein as if set
forth word for word, are fair and reasonable and reflect the minimum deposits necessary to protect
the Utility from undue loss; thus, the “Deposit Chart” is hereby adopted and the deposits reflected
therein are hereby fixed as the deposits to be charged to all customers who establish water and/or
wastewater service with the Utility.

Section 8. Payment by Customers. The monthly bill is payable on the Due Date. Monthly

bills shall be based upon the volume of water and wastewater used and the applicable rate; however,
the monthly bill shall be at least the Minimum Monthly Charge, if any, as reflected on the applicable
rate.

A. Late payment and nonpayment. Any customer who does not pay his or her
bill prior to the close of the regular business day on the Due Date will be sent a late notice and
assessed both a 10% penalty and a re-billing fee. Any customer who does not pay his or her bill
prior to the close of the regular business day on the Cut-off Date will be Disconnected and may be
Locked-off. Any customer whose water service meter has been Disconnected or Locked-off by the
Utility will be assessed a Re-connection fee in addition to any and all past-due amounts, penalties,
and fees. No customer shall be reconnected unless and until all past-due amounts, penalties, and
fees, including the Re-connection fee, have been paid in full.

B. Account Termination. When an account becomes delinquent for 30 days, the
Utility shall mail notice to the location receiving service notifying the customer that the delinquent

account is being terminated. If payment is not received within 10 days, the Utility may terminate
--- page 40 (OCR) ---
the delinquent account and liquidate the customer’s deposit to offset any and all debts owed to the
Utility. The Utility may initiate collection procedures according to Arkansas law to collect any
outstanding debts remaining after application of the deposit. Any customer whose account has been
terminated due to non-payment may be required to pay an increased deposit to re-establish service.

Cc. Insufficient Checks. All returned checks or insufficient funds drafts will be
charged a check service fee as allowed by Arkansas law. If not timely paid, action will be
commenced under the Arkansas Hot Check Law and the service disconnected. All fees and
assessments as set forth in this Ordinance or any amendment thereto shall be applied. If two
returned checks or drafts are received on an account for 2 consecutive months, a letter will be mailed
to the customer stating that only certified funds or cash will be accepted for a period of one (1) year.

Dz. Billing Malfunctions. In the event of a computer hardware or software failure
or other circumstances beyond the control of the Utility, the Commission shall have full discretion
to extend the Due Date and Cut-off Date for a period of time commensurate with the delay of the
monthly billing or late notice processing.

Section 9. Billing Disputes. Billing disputes may be initiated by any customer by contacting
the Utility. Upon receipt of a billing dispute, the Utility shall perform an investigation to compile
relevant facts. Upon completing the investigation, the Utility shall compile a synopsis of the facts,
all findings of its investigation, and all documents submitted by the complainant and forward the
same to the Chairperson of the Commission for a final decision. After considering all relevant
information presented by both the Utility and the complainant, the Chairperson, or the
Chairperson’s designee, shall render a decision regarding the proper amount of the bill.

Section 10. Severability. The provisions of the Ordinance are hereby declared to be

separable and if any provision shall for any reason be held illegal or invalid, such holding shall not
--- page 41 (OCR) ---
affect the validity of the remainder of the Ordinance.
Section 11. Repealer. All parts of previous Ordinances and Resolutions in conflict
herewith are hereby repealed.

Section 12. Other Unaffected Policies. Unless in conflict with the Ordinance, all other

Ordinances, Resolutions, and Utility policies will be unchanged.

1 INTRODUCTION

The Cabot Water and Wastewater Commission DBA Cabot Waterworks has been vested with the
authority and responsibility for the proper operation, maintenance and improvement of the water and
wastewater systems of the City of Cabot pursuant to the authority provided by Arkansas Code
Annotated 88 14-234-116, and 14-234-30 I, et seq.

Cabot Waterworks, located in Cabot, Arkansas, serves a population of 27,515 through 11,127
metered connections as of 12/31/2024. This total includes master meter connections that serve
1,426 multi-unit residential customers and 154 multi-unit commercial customers, such as
apartment complexes and shopping malls. The utility is led by Tim Joyner, P.E., with Bruce Brown as
the Financial Manager. The water system currently sources water from the Alluvial aquifer, with a
maximum intake capacity of 4.0 MGD. Cabot Waterworks also has a purchase agreement with
Central Arkansas Water (CAW). This agreement includes a minimum purchase of 0.3 MGD and a
maximum of 9.0 MGD. The Arkansas Natural Resources Commission has mandated Cabot
Waterworks discontinue its groundwater well operations by 2026. Without other internal water
sources, this change would require Cabot to purchase 100% of its water from CAW. Additionally,
Cabot Waterworks maintains an emergency connection to Jacksonville Waterworks but does not
currently have a purchase agreement in place with Jacksonville.

2.2.3 Current Standings

Cabot Waterworks’ recorded revenue has exceeded its recorded expenses. They also account for
their debt services, which will be further discussed in the next section, along with a 5% gross revenue
repair and refurbish reserve. By incorporating the 5% repair and refurbish reserve while covering their
debt service and operation and maintenance expenses, they are meeting certain requirements of Act
605.

2.3 Water Long-Term Debt Service

Cabot Waterworks entered into a Bond Purchase Agreement on January 13, 2005, to finance the
planning, design, construction, and rehabilitation of the water system in the amount of $8,000,000.

bond is repaid through semiannual installments of $230,119.17, which includes a 1% servicing fee,

total expenses, capital improvements, and the required repair and refurbish reserve, from the total
revenue. This resulting net revenue is then divided by the debt service.

3 BILLED WATER MODEL

The following sections will outline the methodology for projecting the impact of adjustments to the
current rate structure. The model will be validated by applying 2024 consumption and connection
data to the current rate structure and comparing the results to the recorded billed revenue for 2024.

3.1 Water Sold and Number of Connections

Part of projecting the results of a rate adjustment requires determining the amount of water used
(gallons), number of connections per connection type, and the existing rates.

3.1.1 Population and Connections

Connections refer to the number of active meters within the Cabot Waterworks system across all
customer classes. The number of connections is a significant factor in Billed Revenue, as it directly
influences the minimum revenue projected from the debt service fee (Service Flat Charge), which is
charged to each customer regardless of water consumption.

The number of connections can be projected based on population trends. The City of Cabot has
experienced consistent population growth. Since 1970, the city has had an average annual growth
rate of 4.28%, but this rate has slowed to an average of 1.23% over the past decade. Figure 3-1
displays the recorded population from 1970, with a linear trendline to support projections. Using the
1.23% annual growth rate, the orange line in the chart represents the projected population over the
period covered by this rate study.

Two methods were used to project annual consumption, both yielding very similar results. The first
method involved comparing each month from one year to the next to determine the percentage
change in consumption. For instance, February 2015 to February 2016 showed a -0.94% change,
indicating a decrease. This process was repeated for each month across the available data, and the
percentage changes for each month over the past decade (2014-2024) were averaged. The average
percentage change for each month was then applied to the most recent monthly recorded data,
projecting consumption for each month over the study period. The monthly totals were summed to
provide annual consumption projections.

The second approach involved comparing year-to-year consumption changes and calculating the
average percent growth over the past decade. This average growth rate was then applied to the most
recent recorded year's total consumption. Both projection methods produced comparable results,

4.1 Purchased Water

Cabot Waterworks currently relies on groundwater as its primary water source. However, as

transition could require Cabot Waterworks to purchase all of its water supply from Central Arkansas
Water (CAW), which will significantly increase purchase water expenses due to both the higher
volume of purchased water and the scheduled rate increases set by CAW (CAW’s Rate schedule is
provided in the Appendix of this report).

Currently, Cabot Waterworks purchases 0.3 MGD from CAW, which is approximately 11.87% of its
total water use projected for 2025. To assess the financial implications of maintaining this purchase

4.4 Forecasting Revenue v. Expenses

The model methodology outlined in Section 3, for billed revenue projections will be used to compare
forecasted revenue and expenses. Non-rate revenue will be projected with a 3% annual increase, and
this impact is reflected in the updated revenue projections.

e Table 4-4 presents the projected revenue and expenses if Cabot Waterworks transitions to
100% purchased water from CAW.

e Table 4-5 displays the projected revenue and expenses if Cabot Waterworks remains with the
current purchase agreement, continuing to purchase only 0.3 MGD of its total water use from
CAW. Unlike the 100% purchase scenario, O&M expenses will not decrease in this case, as
the costs associated with maintaining the existing groundwater infrastructure will persist.

The financial impact of transitioning to 100% purchased water from CAW versus maintaining the
current purchase agreement presents key differences:

e Transitioning to 100% purchased water significantly increases total expenses due to higher
purchased water volume, scheduled CAW rate increases, and additional fees such as the
Infrastructure Fee, Watershed Protection Fee, and Development Fee. As a result, a larger net
deficit is projected, particularly in 2026 when the full transition takes effect.

e Maintaining the current purchase agreement avoids the higher costs associated with 100%
purchased water by maintaining the existing groundwater system. While this scenario
reduces dependency on CAW’s rate structure, continued investment in infrastructure and
potential capital improvements may still be necessary.

While moving to fully purchased water simplifies operations, it comes at a higher financial cost.
Without rate adjustments, Cabot Waterworks will face growing deficits under both scenarios. Rising
costs for materials, fuel, and maintenance further strain financial stability. To account for inflation
and operational cost growth, a 4% annual increase has been applied to 2024’s recorded O&M
expenses outside of purchased water and public safety, as well as all general and administrative
(G&A) expenses. Public safety expenses will remain at 5% of water billed revenue plus $35,000 in
Lieu of City Taxes, while a 5% gross revenue allocation for repairs and refurbishments will also be
applied.

To maintain financial sustainability, a rate increase will be necessary to cover the rising cost of
purchased water. However, operating expenses, regulatory compliance, and_ infrastructure
investments are adequately funded under the current rate structure, provided there are no changes
to the purchase agreement with CAW.

5 WATER RATE INCREASE

Rising costs across multiple areas—including purchased water expenses, operations, maintenance,
and infrastructure—necessitate a rate adjustment to maintain financial stability. This section
presents two rate results scenarios to address these increasing expenses:

e Section 5.1 outlines the unit rate increase per customer for 100% purchased water
agreement.

e Section 5.2 outlines a rate increase if Cabot Waterworks transitions to purchasing 100% of
its water from CAW.

e Section 5.3 details the rate results if the utility maintains its current purchase agreement with
CAW, continuing to produce most of its water while purchasing a smaller portion.

e Section 5.4 provides a comparative analysis of the resulting average customer bills.

Through the water model projection process, various rate structures can be evaluated to assess their
financial impact. When considering rate adjustments, factors such as the effect on different
customer groups and the need to cover rising expenses—particularly in purchased water, operations,
and maintenance—must be addressed.

One approach is adjusting the unit rate, ensuring revenue aligns with increasing costs tied to water
consumption. Alternatively, incorporating these expenses into the Service Flat Charge, similar to the
debt service fee, may not fully account for the variable nature of purchased water and operational
costs. Another option is implementing targeted fees to address specific cost drivers.

Ultimately, the selected rate adjustments must enable Cabot Waterworks to meet its financial
obligations while maintaining reliable service and infrastructure.

5.1 Unit Rate Increase CAW

Table 5-1 presents the annual unit rate (cost per 1,000 gallons) from CAW, which is added to all
existing unit rate thresholds. This rate increases each year as purchased water costs rise.

To determine the unit cost, the shortfall revenue due to purchased water (Identified in Table 4-4) is
divided by the projected billed water volume and converted to a per-1,000-gallon basis. This ensures
that the necessary rate adjustments are applied to each customer class and unit rate threshold.

ORDINANCE NO. 21 OF 2026

AN ORDINANCE AMENDING THE PERSONNEL POLICIES OF THE CITY OF
CABOT TO ESTABLISH FIRST AMENDMENT RELIGIOUS PROTECTIONS
REGARDING THE WORKPLACE USE OF GENERATIVE AND AGENTIC
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the City Council of the City of Cabot recognizes and respects the First
Amendment rights of all municipal employees to freely exercise their religion without undue
infringement in the workplace; and

WHEREAS, the rapid emergence of advanced technology includes automated systems
capable of replacing human creative and deliberative choices; and

WHEREAS, the global community has recognized the ethical and spiritual challenges of
this transition, as articulated in Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical Magnifica Humanitas, which declares
that "in the era of artificial intelligence, ours is the pressing duty to remain profoundly human";
and

WHEREAS, certain employees may possess sincerely held religious beliefs dictating that
creativity, artistic expression, and independent moral discernment are uniquely divine or human
traits, thereby creating a conscientious objection to being forced to deploy or command
autonomous synthetic systems to execute these functions; and

WHEREAS, the City seeks to accommodate these religious protections while maintaining
a strict commitment to operational efficiency, fiscal responsibility, and high-quality municipal
services for the citizens of Cabot.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
CABOT, ARKANSAS:

SECTION 1: Definitions.

For the purposes of this Ordinance, the following definitions shall apply:

a. "Generative Artificial Intelligence" means any algorithmic system, software, or deep-
learning model designed to autonomously create novel, expressive content, including but
not limited to static imagery, creative writing, graphic design, and musical compositions, in
a manner that directly substitutes for or replaces the creative execution of a human designer,
artist, or writer.

b. "Agentic Artificial Intelligence" means an artificial intelligence system or software
application endowed with a high degree of autonomy, capable of independently generating
its own goals, making systemic decisions, taking actions in digital environments, and
executing workflows with minimal to no real-time human intervention or oversight.

c. "Assistive Technology" means computational tools designed to optimize, correct, or format
human-authored output without replacing primary human agency, intellectual authority, or
creative thought. This includes, but is not limited to, basic automated spellcheckers,
grammar correction software, spreadsheet calculators, and search engine parameters.
--- page 15 (OCR) ---
SECTION 2: Scope and Accommodations.

No employee of the City of Cabot shall be compelled as a condition of employment to utilize,
deploy, or execute tasks through Generative Artificial Intelligence or Agentic Artificial
Intelligence if doing so directly conflicts with the employee’s sincerely held religious beliefs.

An employee objecting to such usage shall submit a written request for a First Amendment
Technological Accommodation to the Human Resources Department, detailing the nature of the
religious objection. The City shall, whenever reasonably possible, provide alternative, traditional
mechanisms for the employee to complete their assigned duties. This Ordinance shall be read and
interpreted as being supplementary to the City’s current policies on religious accommodations and
not in conflict with said policies. Likewise, this Ordinance shall not be read or interpreted as
conflicting with existing law on the First Amendment or accommodations therefor.

SECTION 3: Exemptions and Limitations.

The protections established under this Ordinance are strictly limited by the following structural
guardrails:

a. Quality and Output Standards. An accommodation granted under this Ordinance shall not
be construed to lower, alter, or exempt an employee from the standard performance metrics,
quality benchmarks, or production timelines expected of their peers. Employees utilizing
traditional human workflows must produce a final product that meets or exceeds all standard
departmental requirements. A degradation in work product quality shall remain valid
grounds for standard disciplinary action under the City’s policies.

b. Mandatory Assistive Technology. The protections herein do not extend to Assistive
Technology. Employees may not, under the auspices of this Ordinance, object on religious
grounds to the use of standard office software, infrastructure optimization tools, or routine
technical aids that do not replace human creativity or decision-making agency.

SECTION 4: Severability.

If any provision of this Ordinance or the application thereof to any person or circumstance is held
invalid, such invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of this Ordinance which
can be given effect without the invalid provision or application, and to this end the provisions of
this Ordinance are declared to be severable.

SECTION 5: Emergency

This Ordinance is necessary for the protection of employee constitutional liberties and the orderly
management of city operations, and an emergency is hereby declared. This Ordinance shall
therefore take effect and be in force from and after its passage and approval.

ORDINANCE NO. 21 OF 2026

AN ORDINANCE AMENDING THE PERSONNEL POLICIES OF THE CITY OF
CABOT TO ESTABLISH FIRST AMENDMENT RELIGIOUS PROTECTIONS
REGARDING THE WORKPLACE USE OF GENERATIVE AND AGENTIC
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the City Council of the City of Cabot recognizes and respects the First
Amendment rights of all municipal employees to freely exercise their religion without undue
infringement in the workplace; and

WHEREAS, the rapid emergence of advanced technology includes automated systems
capable of replacing human creative and deliberative choices; and

WHEREAS, the global community has recognized the ethical and spiritual challenges of
this transition, as articulated in Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical Magnifica Humanitas, which declares
that "in the era of artificial intelligence, ours is the pressing duty to remain profoundly human";
and

WHEREAS, certain employees may possess sincerely held religious beliefs dictating that
creativity, artistic expression, and independent moral discernment are uniquely divine or human
traits, thereby creating a conscientious objection to being forced to deploy or command
autonomous synthetic systems to execute these functions; and

WHEREAS, the City seeks to accommodate these religious protections while maintaining
a strict commitment to operational efficiency, fiscal responsibility, and high-quality municipal
services for the citizens of Cabot.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
CABOT, ARKANSAS:

SECTION 1: Definitions.

For the purposes of this Ordinance, the following definitions shall apply:

a. "Generative Artificial Intelligence" means any algorithmic system, software, or deep-
learning model designed to autonomously create novel, expressive content, including but
not limited to static imagery, creative writing, graphic design, and musical compositions, in
a manner that directly substitutes for or replaces the creative execution of a human designer,
artist, or writer.

b. "Agentic Artificial Intelligence" means an artificial intelligence system or software
application endowed with a high degree of autonomy, capable of independently generating
its own goals, making systemic decisions, taking actions in digital environments, and
executing workflows with minimal to no real-time human intervention or oversight.

c. "Assistive Technology" means computational tools designed to optimize, correct, or format
human-authored output without replacing primary human agency, intellectual authority, or
creative thought. This includes, but is not limited to, basic automated spellcheckers,
grammar correction software, spreadsheet calculators, and search engine parameters.
--- page 9 (OCR) ---
SECTION 2: Scope and Accommodations.

No employee of the City of Cabot shall be compelled as a condition of employment to utilize,
deploy, or execute tasks through Generative Artificial Intelligence or Agentic Artificial
Intelligence if doing so directly conflicts with the employee’s sincerely held religious beliefs.

An employee objecting to such usage shall submit a written request for a First Amendment
Technological Accommodation to the Human Resources Department, detailing the nature of the
religious objection. The City shall, whenever reasonably possible, provide alternative, traditional
mechanisms for the employee to complete their assigned duties. This Ordinance shall be read and
interpreted as being supplementary to the City’s current policies on religious accommodations and
not in conflict with said policies. Likewise, this Ordinance shall not be read or interpreted as
conflicting with existing law on the First Amendment or accommodations therefor.

SECTION 3: Exemptions and Limitations.

The protections established under this Ordinance are strictly limited by the following structural
guardrails:

a. Quality and Output Standards. An accommodation granted under this Ordinance shall not
be construed to lower, alter, or exempt an employee from the standard performance metrics,
quality benchmarks, or production timelines expected of their peers. Employees utilizing
traditional human workflows must produce a final product that meets or exceeds all standard
departmental requirements. A degradation in work product quality shall remain valid
grounds for standard disciplinary action under the City’s policies.

b. Mandatory Assistive Technology. The protections herein do not extend to Assistive
Technology. Employees may not, under the auspices of this Ordinance, object on religious
grounds to the use of standard office software, infrastructure optimization tools, or routine
technical aids that do not replace human creativity or decision-making agency.

SECTION 4: Severability.

If any provision of this Ordinance or the application thereof to any person or circumstance is held
invalid, such invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of this Ordinance which
can be given effect without the invalid provision or application, and to this end the provisions of
this Ordinance are declared to be severable.

SECTION 5: Emergency

This Ordinance is necessary for the protection of employee constitutional liberties and the orderly
management of city operations, and an emergency is hereby declared. This Ordinance shall
therefore take effect and be in force from and after its passage and approval.

ORDINANCE NO. 21 OF 2026

AN ORDINANCE AMENDING THE PERSONNEL POLICIES OF THE CITY OF
CABOT TO ESTABLISH FIRST AMENDMENT RELIGIOUS PROTECTIONS
REGARDING THE WORKPLACE USE OF GENERATIVE AND AGENTIC
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the City Council of the City of Cabot recognizes and respects the First
Amendment rights of all municipal employees to freely exercise their religion without undue
infringement in the workplace; and

WHEREAS, the rapid emergence of advanced technology includes automated systems
capable of replacing human creative and deliberative choices; and

WHEREAS, the global community has recognized the ethical and spiritual challenges of
this transition, as articulated in Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical Magnifica Humanitas, which declares
that "in the era of artificial intelligence, ours is the pressing duty to remain profoundly human";
and

WHEREAS, certain employees may possess sincerely held religious beliefs dictating that
creativity, artistic expression, and independent moral discernment are uniquely divine or human
traits, thereby creating a conscientious objection to being forced to deploy or command
autonomous synthetic systems to execute these functions; and

WHEREAS, the City seeks to accommodate these religious protections while maintaining
a strict commitment to operational efficiency, fiscal responsibility, and high-quality municipal
services for the citizens of Cabot.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
CABOT, ARKANSAS:

SECTION 1: Definitions.

For the purposes of this Ordinance, the following definitions shall apply:

a. "Generative Artificial Intelligence" means any algorithmic system, software, or deep-
learning model designed to autonomously create novel, expressive content, including but
not limited to static imagery, creative writing, graphic design, and musical compositions, in
a manner that directly substitutes for or replaces the creative execution of a human designer,
artist, or writer.

b. "Agentic Artificial Intelligence" means an artificial intelligence system or software
application endowed with a high degree of autonomy, capable of independently generating
its own goals, making systemic decisions, taking actions in digital environments, and
executing workflows with minimal to no real-time human intervention or oversight.

c. "Assistive Technology" means computational tools designed to optimize, correct, or format
human-authored output without replacing primary human agency, intellectual authority, or
creative thought. This includes, but is not limited to, basic automated spellcheckers,
grammar correction software, spreadsheet calculators, and search engine parameters.
--- page 9 (OCR) ---
SECTION 2: Scope and Accommodations.

No employee of the City of Cabot shall be compelled as a condition of employment to utilize,
deploy, or execute tasks through Generative Artificial Intelligence or Agentic Artificial
Intelligence if doing so directly conflicts with the employee’s sincerely held religious beliefs.

An employee objecting to such usage shall submit a written request for a First Amendment
Technological Accommodation to the Human Resources Department, detailing the nature of the
religious objection. The City shall, whenever reasonably possible, provide alternative, traditional
mechanisms for the employee to complete their assigned duties. This Ordinance shall be read and
interpreted as being supplementary to the City’s current policies on religious accommodations and
not in conflict with said policies. Likewise, this Ordinance shall not be read or interpreted as
conflicting with existing law on the First Amendment or accommodations therefor.

SECTION 3: Exemptions and Limitations.

The protections established under this Ordinance are strictly limited by the following structural
guardrails:

a. Quality and Output Standards. An accommodation granted under this Ordinance shall not
be construed to lower, alter, or exempt an employee from the standard performance metrics,
quality benchmarks, or production timelines expected of their peers. Employees utilizing
traditional human workflows must produce a final product that meets or exceeds all standard
departmental requirements. A degradation in work product quality shall remain valid
grounds for standard disciplinary action under the City’s policies.

b. Mandatory Assistive Technology. The protections herein do not extend to Assistive
Technology. Employees may not, under the auspices of this Ordinance, object on religious
grounds to the use of standard office software, infrastructure optimization tools, or routine
technical aids that do not replace human creativity or decision-making agency.

SECTION 4: Severability.

If any provision of this Ordinance or the application thereof to any person or circumstance is held
invalid, such invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of this Ordinance which
can be given effect without the invalid provision or application, and to this end the provisions of
this Ordinance are declared to be severable.

SECTION 5: Emergency

This Ordinance is necessary for the protection of employee constitutional liberties and the orderly
management of city operations, and an emergency is hereby declared. This Ordinance shall
therefore take effect and be in force from and after its passage and approval.

WHEREAS, due to violations of the City of Cabot’s Code of Ordinances, the City has

for certain work on real properties located within the city limits to remove/modify noncompliant

A RESOLUTION SUPPORTING THE EXISTING SUSPENSION OF
THE CABOT POLICE DEPARTMENT’S USE OF FLOCK CAMERAS;
SETTING FORTH REVIEW CRITERIA AND PROCEDURES DURING

SAID SUSPENSION; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, on the evening of August 6, 2026, Mayor Kincade announced an immediate
suspension of the Cabot Police Department’s Flock camera program pending further
comprehensive review. The cameras were unplugged and physically covered the next morning
also pending said review; and

WHEREAS, The Cabot City Council wishes to establish certain criteria and procedures for
the Flock camera program review as set forth herein; and

WHEREAS, the City Council hereby expresses support of the suspension of the Flock
camera program and the subsequent review of said program, subject to the criteria and procedures
set forth herein.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: The Cabot City Council hereby approves of the suspension of the
Cabot Police Department’s Flock camera program pending further comprehensive review.
This review should be done according to the following criteria and procedures:

a. The Flock camera program will remain suspended during the entirety of the
review period, during which the Flock cameras will remain unplugged and
covered.

b. The review will be comprehensive and will include, without limitation, the
ways in which Flock cameras have been utilized by the Cabot Police
Department and the security/privacy measures and policies in place governing
the use of said cameras.

c. The review, if not already commenced, will begin immediately upon passage
of this Resolution and may take up to thirty days therefrom.

d. The findings of the review shall be presented to the City Council at a City
Council meeting within sixty days of the passage of this Resolution. At that
meeting, the City Council may take whatever action it deems appropriate
regarding the suspension, reinstatement, or termination of the Cabot Police
Department’s Flock camera program.

present: Mayor Ken Kincade, City Attorney Ben Hooper, and City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy

Committee, at 6:30 pm.

NOMINATING COMMITTEE - Chairman James Reid
Committee Members: Brandon Hillenburg, Kyle Pickard, Corey Spangler

Nothing on the agenda; no action from the committee.

MUNICIPAL SERVICES COMMITTEE - Chairman, Ed Long
Committee Members: James Reid, Matt Webber, Stephen Redd, and Brandon Hillenburg

An Ordinance Approving The Application For A Private Club, Pursuant To A.C.A. §
3-9-222, To Be Located At 34 Cypress Creek Crossing was discussed. Committee
Member James Reid made a motion to forward the item to the full Council for consideration.
Committee Member Stephen Redd seconded the motion. The motion carried by a vote of 5-
0.

A Resolution Supporting the Existing Suspension of the Cabot Police
Department’s Use of Flock Cameras; Setting Forth Review Criteria and
Procedures During Said Suspension; and for Other Purposes was presented by
Committee Member Brandon Hillenburg. Mayor Kincade provided background on the City’s
use of Flock cameras, which began in 2022. He stated that increased national attention
surrounding the technology raised concerns about privacy and the potential for misuse. As
a result, he directed that the cameras be suspended while the City reviews its policies,
procedures, data retention, and use of the system.

Council discussed the suspension, the benefits, and the potential privacy concerns
associated with the technology. Several Council Members questioned whether suspension
was necessary in the absence of any known misuse by the Cabot Police Department. They
asked how the proposed review would be conducted and who would be responsible for
conducting it. Several Council Members questioned why this item did not flow through the
Police and Fire Committee.

Police Chief Dodd and Captain Gibson addressed questions regarding the Police
Department's use of the Flock system. They stated that no audits or internal reviews have
revealed a pattern of misuse by Cabot officers. They explained that Flock is used as an

--- page 2 (OCR) ---
investigative tool and that officers must independently verify information obtained through
the system before taking law enforcement action. They further explained that searches
require a legitimate law enforcement purpose, that system activity can be audited, and that
the Department can determine who conducted the search and the reason given for it. The
Department currently retains Flock data for 30 days, although shorter retention periods are
available. The Department can also restrict access to Cabot Police Department personnel
only.

Council discussed additional safeguards that could be considered as part of the review,
including limiting outside-agency access, reviewing data-retention periods, establishing
additional auditing procedures, including Flock information in regular Police Department
reports, and providing additional information to the public regarding the Department’s use
of the system.

Committee Member Kyle Pickard suggested holding a town hall meeting to provide citizens
with information about the system and to allow them to provide input. Committee Member
Hillenburg stated that his intent in bringing the resolution forward was to generate public
discussion regarding the technology and its use.

Committee Member Ed Long moved to amend the agenda to allow for public input during
discussion of this item rather than at the end of the meeting. Seconded by Committee
Member Stephen Redd, the motion passed by a vote of 5-0. The floor was then opened for
public comment regarding the Flock camera resolution. Citizens spoke both in support of
the law-enforcement benefits of the system and regarding concerns over privacy, access to
collected information, oversight, accountability, data retention, and the potential for misuse.
Several citizens expressed support for a public hearing where the Police Department could
explain the system, its limitations, policies, safeguards, and accountability measures.

Following discussion and public comment, Council considered holding a public hearing
before taking final action on the resolution. Upon advice from City Attorney Ben Hooper
regarding the appropriate procedure, a motion was made by Committee Member Brandon
Hillenburg and seconded by Committee Member James Reid to forward the resolution to the
full Council for further consideration. By roll-call vote, the motion passed unanimously, 5-0.

A Resolution Authorizing The Mayor And City Clerk-Treasurer To Enter Into An
Agreement With The Cabot Parks And Recreation Commission To Support
Repairs To The Therapy Pool At The Cabot Veterans Park Community Center; To

agreements, service and maintenance history, estimated repair costs, and the timeline for
requesting financial assistance from the City. Committee Member Matt Webber motioned,
seconded by Committee Member Brandon Hillenburg, to forward the item to the full Council
for consideration. The motion passed by a vote of 5-0.

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular Meeting of the Cabot City Council
at 8:17 following the Work Session and break. Council Member James Reid led
the prayer, and Council Member Ed Long led the pledge of allegiance.

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present:
James Reid, Stephen Redd, Kyle Pickard, Matt Webber, Brandon Hillenburg,
Ed Long, Corey Spangler, and Maggie Cope. Others present were Mayor
Kincade, City Attorney Ben Hooper, Deputy City Attorney Courtnie Holt, and
City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters

Mr. Long, seconded by Mr. Webber, moved to approve the July 20 minutes.
The motion passed unanimously.

Mr. Redd, seconded by Mr. Hillenburg, moved only to read the legislation by
title. The motion passed unanimously.

CONFIRMED NEW BUSINESS BY VOTE OF THE COUNCIL: Mr. Hillenburg
moved to confirm Agenda Items (a) Ordinance No. 26, (b) Ordinance No. 27, (c)
Resolution No. 34, and (d) Resolution No. 35. The motion was seconded by Mr.
Long and passed unanimously by roll call vote.

ORDINANCE 26 OF 2026 — AN ORDINANCE CREATING, CERTIFYING, AND
CONFIRMING TAX LIENS AGAINST REAL PROPERTIES AT VARIOUS LOCATIONS
WITHIN THE CITY OF CABOT FOR FUNDS EXPENDED TO PAY FOR SERVICES
RENDERED DUE TO CODE VIOLATIONS; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES was read
by title only by City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom. Mr. Long moved to suspend
the second and third readings, seconded by Mr. Redd. Motion passed by a roll
call vote of 7-1. Mr. Pickard voted no. Mr. Reid moved to adopt, seconded by Mr.
Webber. Motion passed by a roll call vote of 7-1. Mr. Pickard voted no.

ORDINANCE 27 OF 2026 — AN ORDINANCE APPROVING THE APPLICATION FOR
A PRIVATE CLUB, PURSUANT TO A.C.A 3-9-222, TO BE LOCATED AT 34
CYPRESS CREEK CROSSING; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES was read by title only
by City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom. Mr. Redd moved to suspend the second
and third readings due to timing and the legislation being considered
administrative, seconded by Mr. Reid. Motion passed by a unanimous roll call
vote. Mr. Redd moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Webber. Motion passed by a
unanimous roll call vote. Mr. Redd moved to adopt the emergency clause due to
timing and financial hardship, seconded by Mr. Hillenburg. Motion passed by a
unanimous roll call vote.

RESOLUTION NO. 34 OF 2026 - A RESOLUTION SUPPORTING THE EXISTING
SUSPENSION OF THE CABOT POLICE DEPARTMENT'S USE OF FLOCK CAMERAS;
SETTING FORTH REVIEW CRITERIA AND PROCEDURES DURING SAID
SUSPENSION; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES was read by title only by City
Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom. Several motions were made and subsequently
rescinded. Council Member Ms. Cope moved to amend the resolution to remove
the language regarding supporting the existing suspension; to provide for the
Chief of Police to review the criteria with a group; and to include language
providing for a town hall meeting on October 19 at 6:30 pm, with the Council
meeting to follow immediately thereafter. The motion was seconded by Council
Member Mr. Hillenburg and passed unanimously with a roll call vote.

RESOLUTION 35 OF 2026 — A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR AND
CITY CLERK-TREASURER TO ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH THE CABOT
PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION TO SUPPORT REPAIRS TO THE
THERAPY POOL AT THE CABOT VETERANS PARK COMMUNITY CENTER; TO
AMEND THE GENERAL FUND OF THE 2026 ANNUAL OPERATING BUDGET TO
PROVIDE FOR SAID AGREEMENT; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES was read by title
only by City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom. Mr. Redd moved to adopt, seconded
by Mr. Hillenburg. Motion passed unanimously with a roll call vote.

City Director Input: Brian Boroughs updated the Council regarding a potential
change to the location of the planned secondary entrance to Game Time. He
explained that the Council previously authorized $200,000+ to reimburse the
Parks and Recreation Commission for construction of the roadway. Following
recent discussions with Lonoke County regarding concerns with the roadway
connecting to Erwin Parkway, the City is exploring relocating the entrance from
its previously planned location near Exit 21 to the north end of the property near
Lyon College. The County is also considering a roundabout in the area and may
partner with the City on the revised roadway.

City Attorney Ben Hooper advised that the Council's previous authorization was
for construction of a secondary entrance to Game Time and did not specify the
exact location of the roadway. He stated that, provided the project remains
within the authorized amount and continues to serve the same purpose,
additional Council approval would not be required. If the cost exceeds the
authorized amount or the purpose of the roadway substantially changes, the
matter would need to return to the Council for consideration.

services; and

rights of those with service dogs in our community is essential; and

Month. The City Council hopes and intends for this Resolution to raise awareness and support of
service dogs and the adults and children in our community who they serve.

1. Administrative Review

The Board of Adjustments may hear and decide appeals where it is alleged there is error in any
decision made by the administrative official in the enforcement of the Zoning Ordinance.

2. Variances

The Board of Adjustment may authorize variances that are not contrary to the public interest
where, due to special conditions, a literal enforcement of the Zoning Ordinance would result in
unnecessary hardship and deprive the owner of any reasonable use of the land or building

involved. A variance shall not be granted unless:

1. The applicant can show that special conditions exist that are unusual to the land, structure,
or building involved and that these conditions are not applicable to other lands, structures or
buildings in the same zoning district.

2. The applicant can show that literal interpretation of the Zoning Ordinance requirements
would deprive the applicant of rights commonly enjoyed by other properties in the same zoning
district.

3. The applicant can show that special conditions do not result from the actions of the

applicant.

4, The applicant can show that granting the requested variance will not grant the applicant any
special privilege that is denied by the Zoning Ordinance to other lands, structures or buildings in

the same district.

5. Nonconforming (grandfathered) or conditional permitted uses, structures or buildings in the
same or other districts shall be considered justification for granting a variance.

6. The reasons set forth in the application justify the granting of the variance.

7. The Board of Adjustment shall issue a variance that is the minimum variance that makes
possible reasonable use of the land, building, or structure.

8. The granting of the variance will be in harmony with the general purpose and intent of the
Zoning Ordinance and will not be injurious to the neighborhood or otherwise detrimental to the

public welfare.
In granting a variance, the Board of Adjustment may specify appropriate conditions and

safeguards that it deems necessary or desirable. Violations of such conditions and safeguards
are a violation of the Zoning Ordinance.
